stem: A cell is placed in a solution, and water moves out of the cell, causing it to shrink. What kind of solution is it?

A mutation changes one base in a gene, but the protein's amino acid sequence is unchanged. What is the best explanation?
options: The mutation shifted the reading frame of the gene.
The mutation happened in a ribosome, not the DNA.
The mRNA corrects the error before translation.
More than one codon can code for the same amino acid.

stem: How many nucleotides make up one codon?
Deleting one nucleotide near the start of a gene usually harms the protein more than substituting one nucleotide. Why?
options: It shifts how every later codon is read.
It removes the entire gene from the chromosome.
It changes the DNA into RNA.
It prevents the gene from being copied at all.

stem: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele. Two parents who are both carriers have a child. What is the probability that the child is also a carrier?
Hemophilia is an X-linked recessive trait. A carrier mother has children with an unaffected father. What is the probability that a son will have hemophilia?

In snapdragons, flower color shows incomplete dominance: RR is red, RW is pink and WW is white. Two pink plants are crossed. What fraction of the offspring will be pink?

Which type of macromolecule forms the basic structure (the bilayer) of cell membranes?

Which element is found in all proteins but not in carbohydrates?
The stomach enzyme pepsin works best at about pH 2. What happens to pepsin's activity when it enters the small intestine, where the pH is about 8?
options: It increases, because higher pH speeds up all reactions.
It stays the same, because enzymes are not used up.
It drops sharply as the pH changes its shape.
It changes into a different enzyme that digests fat.

options: To kill surviving bacteria, which tend to be resistant
To build up a supply of antibiotics in the body for future infections
To help the antibiotic kill any viruses that may also be present
To train the immune system to make its own antibiotics
